summary.assessment: On single-panel figures the model is dependable: the grouped bar chart with printed counts (B1) is exact, and the two interval plots (A3, B4) are within 5 % of the axis range, although the centres carry a constant -0.02 offset in A3 and are rounded to 0.1 in B4. The three pies (C5) are exact too, but they were read by the engine's vector path without any model call. Every multi-panel data figure fails, and mostly by data that never comes back: B2 timed out at 600 s with no output, B3 returned 15 rows without a single value and ignored the printed AUROCs, B5 and C1 left 7 of 9 and 2 of 4 panels 'not read', and C3 found 2 of 22 items; panels are merged or lost in five figures. Where it does measure marks in such figures the numbers are unreliable (C1 bars 0.17 too low, C3 segments off by up to 20 points and one negative), and box-plot whiskers are guessed as symmetric bands. On non-charts it returns no numbers in four of five cases but always wraps the diagram in a chart-typed empty panel, and it turned an ECG trace into a 10-row line series. It can be trusted on a single-panel chart with printed values or a handful of clearly separated marks, and not on multi-panel, stacked or box-plot figures; a call takes 100-400 s, which is what exhausts the per-figure budget.
